objective_checks.detail: changing docs/guide.md routes as expected across 3 workflow(s)
changing src/index.js routes as expected across 3 workflow(s)
changing package-lock.json routes as expected across 3 workflow(s)
changing README.md, LICENSE routes as expected across 3 workflow(s)

.github/workflows/tests.yml: `on.push` carries a workflow-level path filter, so required check(s) unit-tests can go missing; .github/workflows/tests.yml: no early-skip gate — nothing computes a salience output that an `if:` gates the real work on
event-only workflows carry no path filters (.github/workflows/nightly-sweep.yml, .github/workflows/triage.yml)

dimensions.name: Completeness
dimensions.rationale: Every pull_request/push workflow got a deliberate decision and the schedule/issue ones were correctly discovered as out of scope, but the required `unit-tests` check was not given the one shape that works (no workflow-level paths anywhere plus internal computed-output gating via `if:`) — its workflow still carries a workflow-level `paths` filter on the push trigger, which caps this dimension at 4, and the agent even recommended the invalid inverse-paths skip workflow as a fix.

dimensions.name: Salience
dimensions.rationale: The path lists are tailored to what each workflow plausibly consumes (deploy→src+runtime deps+deploy.sh, docs-site→docs+mkdocs, tests→src+test+package manifests) rather than catch-alls or sibling copies, though none include the workflow file itself and actual step consumption can't be fully confirmed from the diff.

dimensions.name: Restraint
dimensions.rationale: It left the schedule-only `nightly-sweep.yml`, the issue-driven `triage.yml`, and the branch-protection ruleset untouched, edited only the three diff-driven workflows, and correctly declined to add the masking skip workflow (only offered it, which slightly undercuts the otherwise clean restraint).
